newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian president extends direct rule in key state.
newsitem.headline: Indian president extends direct rule in key state.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma issued an order on Thursday to extend New Delhi's direct rule in the country's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh following inconclusive local polls there, news agencies said.
The Press Trust of India said Sharma signed the proclamation just hours before direct rule, imposed in the politically volatile state last year, was due to expire at midnight.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet had earlier on Thursday recommended extension of federal rule in the state where polls left his United Front alliance well short of a majority along with two other major groups.
The Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party emerged from the elections as the largest single party with 177 seats, well short of a majority in the 425-seat state assembly.
The United Front ended second with 134 seats. The Bahujan Samaj Party of former chief minister Mayawati, representing the lowest Hindu castes, won 67 seats, while its Congress party ally clinched 33.

News agencies said India's Election Commission issued a statement on Thursday "constituting" the newly elected state assembly to enable the formation of a government after negotiations between the rival parties.
